sentences.text: ?Neutral Citation No. - 2025:Ahc:94551
Court No. - 52
Case :- Application U/S 528 Bnss No. - 16584 of 2025

Applicant :- Shubham And 3 Others
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another

Counsel for Applicant :- Bhriguram Ji,Deo Brat Pandey
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Vikas Budhwar,J.
1.

Heard Sri B.R.J. Pandey, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri S.K. Singh, learned Aga for the
State.

2.  This is an application filed under Section 528 BNSS seeking quashing of the entire proceeding of Case No.185 of 2024 arising out of Case Crime No.44 of 2021, under Section 354, 504, 506, 341 IPC,
P.S. Kerakat, District Jaunpur as well as impugned cognizance order dated 09.09.2024, pending in the Court of A.C.J.M. I, Court No.12, Jaunpur.

3. Learned counsel for the applicants submitted that case of the applicants is that before lodging of the impugned FIR on 26.02.2021 which came to be lodged by the opposite party no.2 against the applicants being FIR No.0044, under Section 354, 354B, 354C 504, 506, 376, 511 IPC.
An FIR had also been lodged by the applicants faction against the opposite party no.2 faction being FIR No.277 of 2020 on 09.08.2020, under Sections 147, 323, 504, 506, 452, 354 IPC.

sentences.text: Submission of learned counsel for the applicant is that the present FIR is nothing but a retaliation to counterblast as prior to it an FIR has been lodged by the applicants faction regarding landed dispute pursuant whereto the female/woman of the applicants faction were subjected to maltreatment and offences under Section 354 IPC along with others.

He submits that even a civil dispute is also pending inter-se between the parties, before the Court of Judicial Magistrate,
Shahganj, Jaunpur in which an interim protection has been accorded in favour of the applicants.

entities.text:
Court of Judicial Magistrate,
Shahganj, Jaunpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Submission is that the allegation so sought to be levelled in the FIR lodged against the applicants that applicants had committed offences while attempting to outrage the modesty of opposite party no.2 and while committing the offences relatable to indecent gestures and behavior, the same are bundles of lies.
5. Learned AGA, on the other hand, submits that it is not a hard and fast rule that any subsequent FIR lodged by the other faction is to be necessarily termed to be a counterblast.

He submits that here cognizable offences are made out from the nature of the allegations and further victim/opposite party no.2 has supported the prosecution theory in her statements under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
6.
I have heard submissions so made across the bar and carefully perused the record.
7. Apparently, an FIR has been lodged levelling allegation against the applicants that they attempted to outrage the modesty of the victim and further exhibited indecent conduct.
The statement of the victim under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. also supports the prosecution theory.
The question as to whether there is any truthness or veracity in the said allegations is a subject matter of trial.

Moreover, though, learned counsel for the applicant may be right in contending that earlier the applicant faction and lodged an FIR is concerned but the same would be of no aid, particularly,
when allegations are serious in that regard.
8.
Moreover, pendency of a civil suit and operation of interim injunction is a question which needs to be considered at the time when the trial commences.
9. Accordingly, no case is made out for interference.
10. At this juncture, learned counsel for the applicants submits that applicants shall be preferring a discharge application.
In case, such such discharge application is preferred then the same shall be decided strictly in accordance with law.

11. Considering the submissions of the rival parties as well as stand taken by them, the application stands consigned to records granting liberty to the applicants to prefer discharge application before the court below then the same shall be considered with most expeditions strictly as per the law of the land.
